subtitle: When the Fifth Guru Wove Many Songs into One Eternal Word

panels.shot: epic low-angle wide of Harmandir Sahib rising from the sarovar at dawn
panels.action: Guru Arjan & Bhai Gurdas stand on the marble edge of the Harmandir Sahib’s causeway, the glimmering shrine reflected in the still sarovar as the sky blushes with first light over Amritsar.

dialogue.text: In the age of Akbar and Jahangir, Guru Arjan and Bhai Gurdas gather scattered songs into the Adi Granth, and a new scripture rises beside the Pool of Nectar.

i18n.hi: अकबर‑जहांगीर के दौर में गुरु अर्जन और भाई गुरदास बिखरे शबद समेटकर आदि ग्रंथ रचते हैं, अमृत‑सरवर के किनारे नया धर्म‑ग्रंथ उठ खड़ा होता है।

panels.shot: wide interior shot of a modest Punjab house in Goindval, morning light slanting in
panels.action: Inside a quiet room in Goindval, Guru Arjan sits cross-legged before low wooden stands with loose pothis and scrolls, while Bhai Gurdas kneels nearby with reed pens and ink ready, attentive to the Guru’s calm gaze.

dialogue.text: Across the rivers of Punjab, the hymns of the Gurus travel by memory and manuscript. Some are true. Some are twisted. Whispers reach Guru Arjan: forged shabads, altered lines, words bent to pride.

i18n.hi: पंजाब की नदियों के पार, गुरुओं के कीर्तन यादों और पोटियों में चलते हैं। कुछ सच्चे, कुछ विकृत। गुरु अर्जन तक फुसफुसाहट पहुँचती है: जाली शबद, बदली हुई पंक्तियाँ, अहंकार से मुरड़े हुए बोल।

panels.shot: medium close-up on Guru Arjan in profile, with Bhai Gurdas slightly behind, listening
panels.action: Guru Arjan leans slightly toward Bhai Gurdas, palm open over a spread of handwritten folios inscribed in different hands, his expression steady yet weighted, while Bhai Gurdas listens, eyes intent and respectful.

dialogue.speaker: Guru Arjan
dialogue.text: The river of naam must not be muddied. We shall gather the true bani.

i18n.hi: नाम की नदी गंदी नहीं होने देंगे। सच्ची बाणी ही जुटाएँगे।

dialogue.text: He sees that songs alone cannot guard themselves. A living path needs a written spine.

i18n.hi: उन्हें दिखता है, गीत अकेले अपना पहरा नहीं दे सकते। जीवंत मार्ग को एक लिखित रीढ़ चाहिए।

panels.shot: over-the-shoulder shot from behind Bhai Gurdas, looking at manuscripts spread in a semicircle
panels.action: From behind Bhai Gurdas, we see Guru Arjan gently sorting worn pothis and loose sheets into ordered piles, each labelled by small wooden markers, as dust motes drift in the light and a faint breeze stirs the edges of the pages.

dialogue.text: From Goindval to Amritsar, early pothis and memories arrive. Old companions recite, singers repeat, and Guru Arjan measures every line against the living echo in the sangat.

i18n.hi: गोइंदवाल से अमृतसर तक पुरानी पोटियाँ और यादें आती हैं। सँगती साथी सुनाते हैं, रागी दोहराते हैं, और गुरु अर्जन हर पंक्ति को संगत की जीवंत गूँज से तौलते हैं।

panels.shot: tight shot on Bhai Gurdas’ hands preparing a fresh folio, with Guru Arjan’s hand pointing gently
panels.action: Bhai Gurdas smooths a fresh folio on a low desk, dipping his reed pen into an inkpot, while Guru Arjan’s hand hovers over the blank surface, ready to dictate, a pile of earlier drafts stacked neatly beside them.

dialogue.text: This is no single copy but the fruit of many drafts. The Guru orders, arranges, reconsiders. Bhai Gurdas writes, revises, and writes again, line upon line.

i18n.hi: यह कोई एक नकल नहीं, कई मसौदों का फल है। गुरु आदेश देते, सजाते, फिर सोचते हैं। भाई गुरदास लिखते, सुधारते, फिर लिखते हैं, पंक्ति दर पंक्ति।

panels.shot: medium two-shot, Guru Arjan dictating, Bhai Gurdas writing with focus
panels.action: Guru Arjan sits upright, eyes half-closed as he chants softly, fingers counting the beats of a raga, while Bhai Gurdas bends over the page, carefully inscribing flowing Gurmukhi letters onto the manuscript.

dialogue.text: He does not gather only his own voice. From the First Guru to the Fourth, the bani of the Gurus is set down, raga by raga, so that melody itself will guard their order.

i18n.hi: वह सिर्फ अपनी आवाज़ नहीं जोड़ते। पहले से चौथे गुरु तक, गुरुओं की बाणी राग‑राग में उतरती है, ताकि राग ही उनकी व्यवस्था का पहरा दे।

panels.shot: montage-like wide shot with translucent overlays of different saintly figures around Guru Arjan
panels.action: Guru Arjan sits at the center, while around him faint, respectful images of Kabir, Ravidas, Namdev and Sheikh Farid appear as ghostly presences, each in their distinct dress, evoking distant bhakti and Sufi worlds converging in his work.

dialogue.text: Then, like distant rivers meeting, the songs of bhagats and Sufis flow in. Kabir from Benares, Ravidas the leatherworker, Namdev the wanderer, Sheikh Farid from the Persianate past. Different tongues. One thirst.

i18n.hi: फिर जैसे दूर‑दूर की नदियाँ मिलें, भगतों और सूफियों के गीत उमड़ आते हैं। बनारस के कबीर, चर्मकार रविदास, फकीर नामदेव, फ़ारसी रंग के शेख फ़रीद। अलग ज़बानें, एक प्यास।

panels.shot: medium shot of Bhai Gurdas pausing his writing, slightly startled, as Guru Arjan gestures inclusively
panels.action: Bhai Gurdas lifts his pen for a moment, looking up with a question in his eyes, while Guru Arjan raises his hand in an open, welcoming gesture, indicating a pile of hymns attributed to non-Sikh saints.

dialogue.speaker: Bhai Gurdas
dialogue.text: Master, voices from so many paths…shall they sit together here?

i18n.hi: स्वामी, इतने राहों की आवाज़ें…क्या सब यहाँ साथ बैठेंगी?

dialogue.text: Bhai Gurdas wonders at the boldness. No court has yet bound such a fellowship in one book.

i18n.hi: भाई गुरदास इस साहस पर चकित हैं। किसी दरबार ने अभी तक इतनी संगत को एक ही किताब में नहीं बाँधा।

panels.shot: close-up on Guru Arjan’s serene face, eyes steady, slight smile
panels.action: Guru Arjan’s face fills the frame, calm and luminous, as he looks slightly past the viewer, hands resting lightly on his knees, the hint of a gentle smile softening his firm decision.

dialogue.speaker: Guru Arjan
dialogue.text: Where there is truth, there is our kin. Let the low and the high sing together.

i18n.hi: जहाँ सच है, वहीं अपना कुल। नीच‑ऊँच सबको संग गाने दो।

dialogue.text: Caste, court, and custom fall away. The measure is only this: does the shabad lead from self to the One?

i18n.hi: जाता, दरबार और रिवाज़ झरते जाते हैं। बस एक तराजू बचता है: क्या यह शबद मन से उठा कर एक में मिला देता है?

panels.shot: overhead shot of a large manuscript folio, with headings marking ragas and different authors
panels.action: From above, we see a wide folio where bold raga headings crown neat columns of script, short author marks indicating Guru and bhagat, as Guru Arjan’s finger traces the structure and Bhai Gurdas adds a careful heading.

dialogue.text: He orders the bani by raga, not by rank. Gurus, bhagats, and Sufis stand in a single musical court, their names noted, their verses woven, so that no forger may easily creep in.

i18n.hi: वह बाणी को राग से सजाते हैं, रुतबे से नहीं। गुरु, भगत, सूफी सब एक ही सुर‑दरबार में खड़े, नाम लिखे, बोल गुँथे, ताकि कोई जालसाज़ चुपके से न घुस सके।

panels.shot: medium shot of both men slightly weary but content, surrounded by stacked folios
panels.action: In a dimmer evening light, Guru Arjan and Bhai Gurdas sit amid piles of completed folios, shoulders relaxed, their faces marked by gentle fatigue, while a small oil lamp flickers beside the thickened manuscript.

dialogue.text: Months lengthen into years. Manuscripts cross the Beas and the Ravi. Early recensions are corrected. Lines polished. The new granth grows heavier in their hands, as if a living presence settles between its covers.

i18n.hi: महीने बढ़कर साल बनते हैं। हस्तलिखित ग्रंथ ब्यास‑रावी पार करते हैं। पुराने रूप सुधरते हैं। पंक्तियाँ निखरती हैं। नया ग्रंथ हाथों में भारी होता जाता, जैसे इसके बीच कोई जीवंत हाज़री उतर आई हो।

panels.shot: wide shot of Amritsar sarovar under construction, with the Harmandir rising at its center
panels.action: The scene opens to Amritsar’s vast sarovar, its embankments busy with workers laying stone, while the Harmandir stands in mid-construction at the center, Guru Arjan and Bhai Gurdas observing from the edge, robes fluttering in the breeze.

dialogue.text: As the book takes shape, so does the house that will hold it. Around the Pool of Nectar, the Harmandir rises low and open, doors to every side, a shrine for a scripture not owned by any one gate.

i18n.hi: किताब का रूप बनता है, तो उसका घर भी। अमृत‑सरवर के चारों ओर हरमंदिर नीचा, खुला, हर दिशा को दरवाज़ा, उस ग्रंथ के लिए धाम जो किसी एक दहलीज़ का नहीं।

panels.shot: slow push-in on the nearly finished Adi Granth resting on a cloth, with hands reverently preparing it
panels.action: The nearly completed Adi Granth rests wrapped in a clean cloth on a low platform; Guru Arjan’s hands carefully smooth the fabric, while Bhai Gurdas kneels to tie the binding cords with reverent concentration.

dialogue.text: By 1604, the labor stands whole enough to be installed. It is not yet a final, frozen text, but a great gathering—Guru, bhagat, Sufi, artisan, farmer—all sheltered in one written sky.

i18n.hi: १६०४ तक यह मेहनत इतनी पूर्ण हो उठती है कि प्रतिष्ठा के योग्य हो जाए। अभी यह आख़िरी, जमी हुई लिपि नहीं, बल्कि एक विशाल संगम है—गुरु, भगत, सूफी, कारीगर, किसान—सब एक लिखित आकाश तले।

panels.shot: large wide-angle shot of the causeway to Harmandir, with a procession carrying the Granth
panels.action: A solemn procession crosses the stone causeway to the Harmandir; Guru Arjan walks barefoot behind attendants who carry the wrapped granth on their shoulders, with Bhai Gurdas just behind, while the sarovar mirrors the gathered sangat lining the water’s edge.

dialogue.text: On a clear day in early September 1604, the Adi Granth enters the Harmandir. Feet are bare, heads are bowed. The sangat hums with shabads as the first great book of the Sikhs crosses the water.

i18n.hi: सितंबर १६०४ की साफ़ सुबह, आदि ग्रंथ हरमंदिर में प्रवेश करता है। पाँव नंगे, सिर झुके। संगत शबद गुनगुनाती है जब सिखों की पहली महान किताब पानी पार करती है।

panels.shot: intimate interior shot inside the Harmandir, low angle on the Granth being placed
panels.action: Inside the Harmandir, lit by soft daylight and oil lamps, Guru Arjan gently guides the granth onto a raised platform, while Bhai Gurdas kneels at the side, hands folded, the tranquil sarovar visible through the open doorway.

dialogue.text: Baba Buddha is appointed the first granthi. The Guru bows before the very words he has arranged, showing the Panth that from this day the Guru’s light will also shine through the shabad on these pages.

i18n.hi: बाबा बुੱਢा पहले ग्रंथी ठहराए जाते हैं। गुरु स्वयं उस बाणी के आगे झुकते हैं जिसे उन्होंने सजाया, दिखाते हुए कि अब से गुरु की जोत शबद के रूप में इन पन्नों से भी चमकेगी।

panels.shot: medium shot of Guru Arjan seated behind the Granth as it is recited, Bhai Gurdas beside him
panels.action: Guru Arjan sits behind the open granth, listening as another Sikh reads aloud from its pages; Bhai Gurdas sits to one side, eyes closed, lips moving softly with the familiar verses, while worshippers listen in stillness.

dialogue.text: The bani is now sung from a single source. The Adi Granth does not end debate or doubt, but it gives the Panth a shared reference, where many voices speak in one remembered tune.

i18n.hi: अब बाणी एक ही स्रोत से उठती है। आदि ग्रंथ बहस या शंका को ख़त्म नहीं करता, पर पंथ को एक सांझा आसरा देता है, जहाँ अनेक आवाज़ें एक याद किए हुए सुर में बोलती हैं।

panels.shot: wide court-like shot suggesting Mughal authority, with Guru Arjan at the center, guards at the edges
panels.action: In a stark, high-ceilinged Mughal hall, Guru Arjan stands calm and unarmed at the center, flanked at a distance by armed guards in imperial livery, while light from lattice windows casts patterned shadows on the floor.

dialogue.text: Yet the same age that nurtures this granth also tightens its imperial fist. Under Jahangir, complaints and suspicions gather. The Guru’s growing authority—and his ties to rebels—draw the eye of the Mughal court.

i18n.hi: पर यही युग, जो इस ग्रंथ को सींचता है, साम्राज्य की मुट्ठी भी कसता है। जहाँगीर के राज में शिकायते और शक्क जमा होते हैं। गुरु की बढ़ती प्रतिष्ठा—और बाग़ियों से नाता—मुग़ल दरबार की नज़र खींच लेते हैं।

panels.shot: medium close-up of Guru Arjan under guard, serene, hands folded
panels.action: Guru Arjan sits on the ground under watchful soldiers, his hands folded in his lap, face peaceful despite confinement, while in the background the faint outline of Lahore’s skyline hints at the city beyond.

dialogue.text: In 1606, Jahangir records that Arjan was seized and died in custody. Sikh memory keeps more: that the Fifth Guru refused to alter his granth or the path it enshrined, accepting suffering rather than bending the shabad.

i18n.hi: १६०६ में जहाँगीर लिखता है कि अर्जन पकड़े गए और हवालात में मरे। सिख स्मृति और कहती है: पाँचवें गुरु ने अपना ग्रंथ या उसमें बसे मार्ग को बदलने से इनकार किया, शबद झुकाने से बेहतर दुःख स्वीकारा।

panels.shot: symbolic wide shot of Harmandir at dusk, Granth silhouetted inside, Bhai Gurdas in foreground
panels.action: At dusk, the Harmandir glows with lamps, the silhouette of the open granth visible through its doorway; in the foreground on the causeway, Bhai Gurdas stands alone, looking toward the shrine, his figure small against the luminous temple and darkening sky.

dialogue.text: Guru Arjan’s body is gone, but his gathered word remains. From that day, the Sikhs remember him as their first martyr, and the Adi Granth as the house where many voices still breathe as one.

i18n.hi: गुरु अर्जन का शरीर चला गया, पर उनकी संजोई वाणी रहती है। उसी दिन से सिख उन्हें पहला शहीद याद करते हैं, और आदि ग्रंथ को वह घर, जहाँ अनेक आवाज़ें आज भी एक साँस में जीवित हैं।

title_i18n.en: Guru Arjan Gathers the Many Voices
title_i18n.hi: गुरु अर्जन ने जोड़ी अनगिनत आवाज़ें

subtitle_i18n.en: When the Fifth Guru Wove Many Songs into One Eternal Word
subtitle_i18n.hi: पांचवें गुरु ने कई गीत बुनकर बनाया एक सनातन शब्द
